This is the closing calls lesson. We'll go through the call stages and the three most common objections.
The call has five stages. Rapport, discovery, gap, offer, and next step.
Rapport is short. Two minutes. Use something from the pre-call brief so they know you listened.
Discovery is the longest stage. Ask about their goal, their current numbers, what they've tried, and why now.
The gap is where you play back the difference between where they are and where they want to be.
Only when the gap is clear do you present the offer.
Now objections. The first one is I need to think about it.
When someone says I need to think about it, ask what specifically they want to think through. Usually it's money, time, or trust.
The second one is it's too expensive.
When someone says it's too expensive, go back to the gap. Compare the price to the cost of staying where they are for another year.
Never discount on the call to close. Discounting teaches them your price isn't real.
The third one is I need to ask my partner.
When someone needs to ask a partner, offer to book a short follow-up call with both of them together.
